name: Kim Bong Carpentry Village
summary: The carpentry village on the south bank of the Thu Bồn, opposite the old town, in what was Cẩm Kim. The heritage page dates the village to about the 16th century and names four trades: building wood, household wood, boats, and decorative carving. It was listed as national intangible heritage on 21 November 2016. The ticket price and the crossing time are check on arrival.
timeNeeded: A morning. Exact minutes are check on arrival.
getThere: Cross the river to Cẩm Kim. The minutes are check on arrival.

body: Kim Bồng sits on the right bank of the lower Thu Bồn, opposite the ancient town, in what the 2011 heritage page calls xã Cẩm Kim. The page dates the village to about the 16th century. The work that is still practised is in four lines: wood for buildings, wood for the house, boatbuilding, and decorative carving. The old town’s carved houses, including Quân Thắng, are the work this village is credited with.

The page says you can see the craft display, watch a demonstration, visit the boatyards, and try a cut. On 21 November 2016 the ministry listed the village as national intangible heritage, Decision 4036/QĐ-BVHTTDL. A May 2018 heritage note had already named it as a recognised local tourism site.

The page says to buy a ticket and does not print the figure, so the price is check on arrival. It also does not print the minutes or the fare for the crossing. Go in the morning. This is not a beach and not a hall on Trần Phú.

gettingThere: The village is across the Thu Bồn from the old town. The heritage page does not print a ferry fare or a minute count. Both are check on arrival.
